records.title: ABS Modulator and Traction Control System Failure
records.description: The Teves Mark IV ABS modulator assembly develops internal leaks and electronic failures, disabling ABS and traction control. The modulator is expensive and integrates the hydraulic pump, valves, and electronic controller into one unit. Moisture intrusion into the electrical connector accelerates failure.
records.solution: The ABS modulator can be sent to a specialty rebuilder for significantly less than dealer replacement cost. Apply dielectric grease to all electrical connectors during reinstallation. Bleed the ABS system using a scan tool to cycle the pump and valves. Inspect the wheel speed sensors and tone rings during the repair.
symptoms: ABS light on
Traction control disabled message
Brake pedal drops under ABS activation
ABS motor runs continuously for short periods

records.title: Climate Control Head Blank Display and Unresponsive Buttons
records.description: The dash-mounted electronic dual-zone climate control head on late-1990s Eldorados commonly goes blank or shows dashes, with buttons becoming intermittent or dead, due to aged electronic components and failing solder joints inside the unit. The HVAC system often keeps running in its last commanded mode, leaving the driver unable to change temperature or fan settings. New OEM control heads are discontinued, so used units or bench repair are the practical fixes.
records.solution: First run the built-in HVAC diagnostics (ignition on, press OFF + WARMER together) and check the HVAC fuse to rule out power or sensor faults; if the head itself is dead, install a known-good used OEM control head or send the unit to an electronics rebuilder. Typical cost is $100-$400 including a used part and installation.
symptoms: Climate control display blank or showing dashes
Buttons unresponsive or only working intermittently
Display cuts in and out with cabin temperature changes
HVAC stuck on the last temperature and fan setting
Backlighting dead while heat or A/C still blows

records.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor Failure Causing Intermittent Stalling and No-Start
records.description: The dual crankshaft position sensors on the 2000-2002 Northstar (which feed the coil-on-plug PCM directly) develop cracked solder joints at an internal resistor, causing intermittent chuggle, stalling while driving, long cranking, or a hot no-start that often resolves once the engine cools. GM ran a voluntary emissions campaign on certain 2000 Eldorado and Seville 4.6L vehicles for this defect, and RepairPal documents it as a top Eldorado driveability problem. Because both sensors live behind the oil filter adapter and fail similarly, the accepted practice is replacing both at once.
records.solution: Replace both crankshaft position sensors (A and B) together, then perform the CKP system variation relearn with a Tech II-type scan tool. Typical independent-shop cost is roughly $200-$500 for both sensors including labor.
symptoms: Intermittent stalling while driving, often restarting after the engine cools
Long crank time or no-start when hot
Engine chuggle or stumble at speed
Check engine light with crank-sensor codes such as P0335 or P0385
Tachometer drops to zero just before the stall

records.title: Electronic Level Control (ELC) Compressor and Air Shock Failure Causing Rear Sag
records.description: The Eldorado's self-leveling rear suspension uses an electric air compressor, height sensor, and air-adjustable rear shocks. Aging air shocks and lines develop leaks that force the compressor to run constantly until its internal dryer clogs with moisture and the pump burns out or seizes, leaving the rear end sagging. RepairPal documents the auto level ride compressor as a known Eldorado failure, and forum diagnostic threads consistently stress that leaks must be fixed first or the replacement pump will die the same way.
records.solution: Find and repair air leaks first (shocks and lines are the usual culprits), then replace the compressor and dryer if the pump no longer builds pressure. Many owners replace the worn air shocks at the same time; budget roughly $250-$900 at an independent shop depending on how many components are replaced.
symptoms: Rear end sits noticeably low, especially with passengers or trunk cargo
Compressor hum behind the rear seat runs constantly or never runs at all
Bouncy, wallowing, or harsh rear ride
Rear suspension bottoms out over bumps when loaded
Vehicle leans or fails to re-level after loading

records.title: Northstar Cold-Start Carbon Knock (Carbon Rap / Piston Slap Noise)
records.description: The Northstar's tight piston-to-head squish clearance lets carbon deposits build up on the piston crowns and combustion chambers, especially in cars driven gently on short trips. When cold, the piston rocks against the carbon and produces a rhythmic rap that sounds alarmingly like rod knock or piston slap but fades as the engine warms. GM addressed it with an induction carbon-cleaning procedure, and in severe persistent cases TSB 03-06-01-025 (covering 2000-2002 Eldorado) authorized piston replacement.
records.solution: Decarbonize the combustion chambers with GM Top Engine Cleaner per the GM service procedure, then perform periodic wide-open-throttle accelerations to keep carbon from re-accumulating. Only rare, severe cases that persist after cleaning warrant the piston replacement described in TSB 03-06-01-025.
symptoms: Rhythmic knock or rap on cold start that fades as the engine warms
Noise most noticeable after extended short-trip, light-throttle driving
Sounds like piston slap or rod knock when cold, quiet when hot
Noise diminishes after a few hard wide-open-throttle accelerations

records.title: Northstar 4.6L V8 Head Bolt/Head Gasket Failure
records.description: The 1993-2002 Eldorado was one of the first vehicles to receive the Northstar 4.6L V8 and has the same head bolt/head gasket failure. Early Northstar engines (1993-1995) are particularly prone as the design was less refined. The Eldorado ETC (Touring Coupe) uses the high-output 300hp Northstar. Same failure mechanism and repair as all Northstar-powered Cadillacs.
records.solution: Engine removal and head stud/Time-Sert installation. Given the age and value of Eldorados, many owners must weigh repair cost ($3-6k) against vehicle value. Eldorado enthusiasts still perform the repair for collector vehicles.
symptoms: Coolant loss with no visible external leak
White smoke from exhaust
Overheating
Milky oil residue
Bubbles in coolant overflow

records.title: Northstar V8 Chronic Oil Leaks (Rear Main Seal and Lower Crankcase Half-Case Seal)
records.description: Beyond its famous head gasket woes, the Northstar 4.6L V8 is notorious for external oil leaks from its two-piece crankcase design. The block is split into upper and lower halves sealed with anaerobic sealant, and as the engine ages this case-half seal, the rear main seal, valve cover gaskets, and oil pan seal all weep or drip. Rear main seal oil drips directly onto the hot exhaust crossover pipe, causing burning-oil odors, and case-half leaks require engine removal to repair properly on the transverse Eldorado.
records.solution: Minor leaks (valve covers, oil pressure sensor) are inexpensive gasket jobs; rear main seal replacement runs roughly $600-$800. A leaking lower crankcase half-case seal requires pulling the engine and resealing, commonly quoted at $2,000-$2,500, so many shops recommend a comprehensive reseal of all seals while the engine is out.
symptoms: Oil spots on the driveway after parking
Burning-oil smell from the exhaust crossover area after driving
Oil film coating the lower engine, pan rails, and bellhousing
Oil level drops between changes with no visible exhaust smoke
Drips concentrated at the rear of the engine near the transaxle

records.title: Nylon Fuel Rail Cracking and Fuel Leak Fire Risk (NHTSA Recall 04V110)
records.description: The 1995-1997 Northstar engines used nylon fuel rails whose tubing degrades and cracks from the combined effects of heat, time, alcohol-blended fuel, pressure cycling, and design stress, allowing pressurized fuel to leak into the engine compartment. In the presence of an ignition source the leak can cause an underhood fire. GM recalled the 1995-1997 Cadillac Eldorado, Seville, and DeVille Concours (4.6L V8) under NHTSA campaign 04V110, ultimately covering roughly 483,000 vehicles, and dealers replaced the nylon rail with a stainless steel unit.
records.solution: Check the VIN for completion of recall 04V110; GM dealers replace the nylon fuel rail with a stainless steel rail (and a revised fuel return line where applicable) free of charge. Any surviving car still on the original nylon rail should have it replaced promptly given the fire risk.
symptoms: Strong fuel odor in or around the engine compartment
Visible fuel wetness or seepage on the fuel rail or return line
Fuel dripping under the engine bay after running
Hard starting or fuel pressure loss in advanced cases

records.title: Water Pump Drive Belt and Tensioner Pulley Failure Causing Sudden Overheating
records.description: The Northstar drives its water pump off the intake camshaft with a short dedicated belt and spring tensioner behind a cover at the rear of the engine, separate from the main accessory belt. The tensioner pulley bearing dries out and seizes or disintegrates with age, which shreds the belt and can melt the plastic cam-driven pulley, instantly stopping all coolant circulation. Because a Northstar that is driven while overheating quickly cooks its head gaskets, a $25 pulley can become a multi-thousand-dollar engine job if the temperature warning is ignored.
records.solution: Replace the water pump drive belt and tensioner pulley (and the cam-driven pulley if it melted); many owners replace the tensioner preventively around 75,000-100,000 miles since parts are cheap and access is straightforward. Stop driving immediately at any sign of overheating to protect the head gaskets.
symptoms: Sudden overheating with the temperature gauge spiking
Squeal, chirp, or rattle from the water pump belt cover at the rear of the engine
Shredded belt fragments found under the small belt cover
Steam or boiling coolant despite the main accessory belt being intact
Heater output goes cold as coolant stops circulating
